findings.rationale: NE's local performance is abnormal from round 1 onward: AUC about 0.57, observed prevalence about 0.36 against a mean predicted risk of about 0.16, and CITL strongly negative at round 20. The federation pooled prevalence is about 0.155, and the other clients sit near AUC 0.8. Inflated prevalence with a collapsed AUC is the label-noise signature (flipped outcomes). Its updates are also anomalous: the norm ratio grows from about 1.5 to about 8.9 and the cosine to the median is near -1 in most rounds. That is consistent with a client training against the federation on corrupted labels, not with a clean client. The subgroup O/E ratios (about 2 in both sexes) point the same way.

OH shows the same label-noise pattern from round 1: AUC about 0.56, prevalence about 0.37 against a mean predicted risk of about 0.18, and CITL about -0.19 at round 20. Its ECE is about 0.20, and its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio about 6.5, mean cosine about -0.85). Subgroup O/E ratios are about 2 in both sex groups and in income groups 5 and 6.

WI matches the label-noise signature from round 1: AUC about 0.56, prevalence about 0.36 against a mean predicted risk of about 0.18, and CITL about -0.18 at round 20. Its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio about 5.9, mean cosine about -0.82), and its subgroup O/E ratios are about 2 in both sex groups.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income) and attribution_churn, then ran narrower follow-ups on NE, GU, round-1 performance, and drift/feature checks for AL, NV, GU, PR, VI, DC. Three clients (NE, OH, WI) stand out consistently: local AUC about 0.56, observed prevalence about 0.36 against predicted risk about 0.17, strongly negative CITL, and anomalous updates (norm ratio 6-9x median, cosine near -0.9) from round 1 onward. I classify these as label_noise with onset round 1. No drift was confirmed: the per-round shift spikes for AL, NV, GU, PR, VI and DC were isolated, not persistent. The feature-summary outliers (e.g. DC BMI, AL Sex) did not replicate at higher resolution and are noise. GU's erratic small-client updates and the subgroup O/E outliers in small clients (VA, IL, WV, GA) look like small-sample noise rather than a persistent fault, so I did not report them. Budget is fully spent (0.0 left).
